questions.question_text: What is the primary way that TOEFL iBT scores help students?
options: They guarantee admission to any chosen university.
They provide confidence for pursuing global opportunities.
They replace the need for academic coursework.
They offer free travel to study destinations.
questions.explanation: The text states that TOEFL iBT scores give students the confidence to pursue opportunities anywhere.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about the acceptance of TOEFL iBT scores?
options: They are accepted by 13,000+ institutions in over 160 countries.
They are accepted only by universities in the United States.
They are only accepted by a few select institutions.
They are not widely recognized by global universities.
questions.explanation: Multiple sections of the provided text confirm that the test is recognized by over 13,000 institutions across more than 160 countries.

questions.question_text: What does the TOEFL iBT Reading section measure?
options: The ability to speak fluently in a classroom.
The ability to write complex academic essays.
Academic skills including understanding passages and vocabulary.
The ability to listen to announcements and summarize them.
questions.explanation: According to the test structure, the Reading section involves tasks like completing words, reading in daily life, and reading academic passages.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of the Reading section of the TOEFL iBT?
options: To test your ability to understand complex academic texts
To measure how fast you can read aloud
To evaluate your vocabulary in everyday conversations
To see how well you can write a summary of a news article
questions.explanation: The Reading section is specifically designed to assess English skills used in university-level research and coursework.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a focus of the Reading section?
options: Analyzing academic passages
Completing sentences with the correct words
Reading materials related to daily life
Listening to lectures for detailed information
questions.explanation: Listening to lectures is a component of the Listening section, not the Reading section.

questions.question_text: What does a 'Complete the Words' task in the Reading section require?
options: Writing a full essay based on a single word
Filling in missing information in a text
Listening to a recording and transcribing it
Speaking about a word's definition
questions.explanation: This task tests your understanding of context and vocabulary by asking you to fill in appropriate words within a reading passage.

questions.question_text: How many Reading tasks should a student expect on the test?
options: Exactly 10
Approximately 50
Over 100
None
questions.explanation: The test specifications indicate approximately 50 items for the Reading section.

questions.question_text: Why are academic passages included in the Reading section?
options: To confuse students with difficult topics
To measure skills required for college-level study
To entertain the reader with fiction
To test how well students can ignore text
questions.explanation: The test aims to replicate real academic environments, so academic passages help universities assess if a student can handle their coursework.

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of the TOEFL iBT Reading section?
options: To test your creative writing skills
To assess how well you understand academic English passages
To measure your ability to speak with native speakers
To evaluate your knowledge of current events
questions.explanation: The Reading section is specifically designed to measure academic English reading comprehension skills as they are used in college classrooms.

questions.question_text: What does a 'Complete the Words' task require you to do?
options: Translate words into your native language
Select the correct words to finish a sentence or passage
Write an essay based on a list of words
Pronounce words clearly into a microphone
questions.explanation: The 'Complete the Words' task focuses on reading context to identify appropriate word choices.

questions.question_text: Why are academic-style passages used in this section?
options: Because they are easier to read than novels
To simulate the type of reading material you will encounter in university courses
To test your historical knowledge of various topics
To encourage you to write your own academic articles
questions.explanation: Academic passages ensure the test accurately reflects the real-world English skills needed for university-level coursework.

questions.question_text: What is NOT a primary objective of the Reading section?
options: Assessing vocabulary knowledge in context
Evaluating understanding of main ideas
Testing your ability to interpret complex academic text
Measuring your speed in typing long sentences
questions.explanation: Typing speed is not a measured skill in the Reading section, which focuses on comprehension.

questions.question_text: How many items should a test taker generally expect in the Reading section?
questions.explanation: The test specifications indicate there are 50 items in the Reading section.

questions.question_text: If you skip all questions in the Reading section, what happens?
options: The section is ignored, but other sections are scored
You receive a low but passing score
The entire test is not scored
You are given extra time at the end
questions.explanation: You must complete at least one question in each section for the test to be valid and scored.
